chapter: Later ventures, lodges and San Francisco recollections
title: Why Music Town opened and how the war ended the bootblack chair
summary: Music picked up around 1940 after the Depression; the war made materials and motors too costly, so the chair project ended and Music Town began.

story.theme_name: Making a living: hard times, day jobs and scarce work
story.community_name: The Depression years and the WPA band

blocks.x: What made you suddenly decide to open Music Town? How did that come about?

Well, music begun to pick up a little bit. See, all during the depression, there wasn't...a musician wasn't nothin', you know...couldn't get no money for it. And around '40, things begin to pick up, you see. And, so after I fooled around with my brother five or six months, I figured I'd have to go back to school again and another...

spend another six months in school, you know, because I'd been out six or eight or nine months, and I...fooling around with him, helping him get this together and then took it all back to New York, stopped in Chicago and Detroit and all around with these things I did, and I had ...oh, a lot of people wanted to buy 'em, you see, but then when I... by the time I got back to Los Angeles, the Japanese War was going on.

You couldn't get no stock. You couldn't...not nothing. And the motors, we could build them for about fifty-five dollars before I left, and come back, the motors almost cost fifty-five dollars. So we just didn't fool with it after that.
